result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Reviewed complete production security configuration, logging statements, properties, Docker Compose, .env.example, Oracle initialization, and Azure scripts. No actual credential values are included in this assessment.

CWE-259/CWE-798 NOT_FOUND: SecurityConfig.java:34-41 obtains the admin password via configuration and hashes it with BCrypt. application.properties:14 and application-docker.properties:5 reference the datasource environment variable; docker-compose.yml:7,9,34,36 requires environment credentials. .env.example:6,12,17 contains explicitly documented placeholders, not real credentials. A default username alone is not a hard-coded authentication secret.
CWE-321 NOT_FOUND: no fixed cryptographic key found; azure-setup.ps1:18-22 uses RandomNumberGenerator and disposes it; passwords at 39,41 come from the environment or generated values.

CWE-732 NOT_FOUND: no confirmed unintended ACL grant established. Oracle grants at oracle-init/01-create-user.sql:16-26 are schema-scoped rather than DBA/ANY privileges. SecurityConfig.java:56 requires authentication for writes; public read access is explicitly intended at 19-20,57-58.

azure-setup.ps1:283-299 writes credentials to .env without explicitly setting an ACL; actual inherited filesystem permissions were not inspected, so unintended readability is a coverage limitation rather than a confirmed permission-assignment finding. Environment credentials and command-line transport were not printed or copied into artifacts.

No live credential validation, historical Git-secret scan, deployed filesystem ACL inspection, or external audit-pipeline verification was performed. Tests are excluded from production credential findings.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging

evidence.explanation: SecurityConfig enables Basic authentication for upload/delete, but production source supplies no authentication success/failure audit listener, failure handler, access-log configuration, or security audit event recorder. Rejected Basic-auth requests are handled before controllers and therefore never reach the existing upload/delete logs. Those mutation logs also record only filename/photo ID, not the authenticated principal or request origin (DetailController.deletePhoto:69; PhotoServiceImpl.uploadPhoto:179-180 and deletePhoto:212). Thus important security events and attribution are absent from application-owned audit logging. An external proxy/SIEM may add coverage, but none is evidenced in repository configuration.

values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
